sentences.text: Ngwevu is a massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived in the Lower Jurassic of South Africa.
The genus is known from a single fossil specimen, cataloged as BP/1/4779, and is distinguished by a unique set of 16 traits, including a ridge on the backside of the jugal bone.
Histological studies indicate the holotype was an adult approximately 10 years old when it fossilized.
The only known specimen was discovered in 1978 by James William Kitching on Tevrede Farm in the Fouriesburg district of South Africa.
Ngwevu was originally thought to be a specimen of Massospondylus but was reclassified as a new genus and species in 2019.
The wider snout of Ngwevu suggests it had a more generalist diet compared to the more selective Massospondylus carinatus.
Ngwevu likely had a stronger bite than Massospondylus carinatus due to its robust jaw and skull features, suggesting they occupied different ecological niches.
Phylogenetic analysis places Ngwevu within the family Massospondylidae.

Ngwevu fossils are found in the Clarens Formation, which has been dated to the Pliensbachian to early Toarcian stages, while other estimates place the animal between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
